```{r}
#| label: setup
library(eurostat)
library(ggplot2)
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(brand.yml)
library(marquee)
library(systemfonts)

# gt tables in Word: see the file for why
source("brand/gt-word.R")

nights <- get_eurostat("tour_occ_nim",
  filters = list(geo = "EU27_2020", unit = "NR",
                 nace_r2 = "I551-I553", c_resid = "TOTAL"))
nights <- na.omit(nights)
latest <- nights[which.max(nights$time), ]
year_ago <- nights[nights$time == seq(latest$time, by = "-1 year", length.out = 2)[2], ]
change <- latest$values / year_ago$values - 1

millions <- label_number(accuracy = 0.1, scale = 1e-6, suffix = " million")
pct <- label_percent(accuracy = 0.1, style_positive = "plus")
month <- format(latest$time, "%B %Y")

# Colours of the five classes of change, from the institute's _brand.yml
brand <- read_brand_yml()
classes <- c("below -2" = "drop", "-2 to 0" = "dip", "0 to 2" = "flat",
             "2 to 5" = "gain", "5 or more" = "surge")
class_colours <- vapply(classes, brand_color_pluck, "", brand = brand)
ink <- brand_color_pluck(brand, "foreground")
slate <- brand_color_pluck(brand, "secondary")
burgundy <- brand_color_pluck(brand, "primary")

# Brand fonts for the figures: systemfonts reads them from ./fonts
if (!dir.exists("fonts")) {
  get_from_google_fonts("Source Sans 3", dir = "fonts")
  get_from_google_fonts("Source Serif 4", dir = "fonts")
}
register_variant("Source Serif 4 SemiBold", "Source Serif 4", weight = "semibold")

theme_nso <- function(base_size = 12) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, base_family = "Source Sans 3") +
    theme_brand_ggplot2(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_marquee(family = "Source Serif 4 SemiBold", colour = ink,
                                   size = rel(1.35), width = 1),
      plot.subtitle = element_marquee(colour = slate, width = 1,
                                      margin = margin(b = 10)),
      plot.caption = element_text(colour = slate, hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 10)),
      plot.title.position = "plot", plot.caption.position = "plot",
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left"
    )
}

# The headline of each figure is computed, like every other number
this_year <- as.integer(format(latest$time, "%Y"))
record <- latest$values == max(nights$values)
trend_headline <- paste(month, if (record) "set a new record" else "stayed below the record")
```

::: {#kf-nights}
[`r millions(latest$values)`]{style="font-size: 2.4em; font-weight: bold; color: #7a1f3d;"}

nights spent at tourist accommodation in the EU in `r month`,
[`r pct(change)`]{style="font-weight: bold;"} compared with a year earlier.

Nights in the EU, `r month`
:::

::: {.column-margin}
**Nights spent** count every night a guest stays in hotels, holiday
accommodation and campsites (NACE I55.1 to I55.3), whatever the guest's
country of residence.
:::

## The EU as a whole {#sec-eu}

`r if (record) paste("No month on record had more nights than", month) else paste(month, "stayed below the record")`.
@fig-trend compares this year with the four previous years;
@sec-countries looks at each country and @sec-methods explains the figures.

```{r}
#| label: trend-data
nights$year <- as.integer(format(nights$time, "%Y"))
nights$month <- as.integer(format(nights$time, "%m"))
past <- nights[nights$year %in% (this_year - 4):(this_year - 1), ]
band <- aggregate(values ~ month, past, \(v) c(lo = min(v), hi = max(v)))
band <- data.frame(month = band$month, band$values / 1e6)
now <- nights[nights$year == this_year, ]
last <- now[which.max(now$month), ]
above <- sum(now$values / 1e6 > band$hi[match(now$month, band$month)])
peak <- month.name[band$month[which.max(band$hi)]]
# Alt text: chart type, axes, then the key pattern, all computed
trend_alt <- paste0(
  "Line chart. Months from January to December along the x-axis, nights spent ",
  "at tourist accommodation in the EU in millions along the y-axis, from zero. ",
  "A burgundy line for ", this_year, ", from January to ", month.name[last$month],
  ", is drawn over a light band giving the lowest and highest value of each month ",
  "from ", this_year - 4, " to ", this_year - 1, ". The ", this_year,
  " line is above the band in ", above, " of its ", nrow(now), " months. ",
  "Nights peak every year in ", peak, "; ", month, " is labelled with ",
  millions(latest$values), ".")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-trend
#| column: page-right
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-width: !expr if (knitr::is_html_output()) 8.5 else 7
#| fig-height: !expr if (knitr::is_html_output()) 4.2 else 3.8
#| fig-cap: !expr trend_headline
#| fig-alt: !expr trend_alt
ggplot(mapping = aes(month)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = band, aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = class_colours[["0 to 2"]]) +
  geom_line(data = now, aes(y = values / 1e6), colour = burgundy, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(data = last, aes(y = values / 1e6), colour = burgundy, size = 3) +
  geom_text(data = last, aes(y = values / 1e6, label = millions(values)),
            hjust = -0.1, size = 4, fontface = "bold", colour = burgundy,
            family = "Source Sans 3") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb, expand = expansion(add = 0.3)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = " m"), limits = c(0, NA),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(subtitle = paste0("Nights spent at tourist accommodation in the EU: ",
                         "{", burgundy, " **", this_year, "**} against the ",
                         "{", class_colours[["5 or more"]], " **range of ",
                         this_year - 4, "-", this_year - 1, "**}"),
       caption = "Source: Eurostat (tour_occ_nim). 2021 and earlier left out (Covid-19).",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_nso()
```

## Countries {#sec-countries}

```{r}
#| label: countries-data
geos <- c("EU27_2020", "IT", "FR", "ES", "DE", "EL", "HR", "NL", "AT")
countries <- get_eurostat("tour_occ_nim",
  filters = list(geo = geos, unit = "NR",
                 nace_r2 = "I551-I553", c_resid = "TOTAL"))
countries <- as.data.frame(countries[countries$time %in% c(year_ago$time, latest$time), ])
tab <- reshape(countries[, c("geo", "time", "values")],
               idvar = "geo", timevar = "time", direction = "wide")
names(tab) <- c("Country", "before", "now")
tab$change <- 100 * (tab$now / tab$before - 1)
tab$Country <- label_eurostat(tab$Country, dic = "geo",
                              custom_dic = c(EU27_2020 = "European Union"))
tab <- tab[order(-tab$change), ]
top <- tab[1, ]
bottom <- tab[nrow(tab), ]
```

@tbl-countries ranks the largest destinations by their change over the year:
`r top$Country` recorded the strongest change (`r pct(top$change / 100)`) and
`r bottom$Country` the weakest (`r pct(bottom$change / 100)`).
@fig-map shows every country with data.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-countries
#| tbl-cap: "Nights spent at tourist accommodation by country, millions"
#| classes: plain
gt(tab) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(before, now), scale_by = 1e-6, decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_number(columns = change, decimals = 1, force_sign = TRUE) |>
  cols_label(before = format(year_ago$time, "%b %Y"),
             now = format(latest$time, "%b %Y"),
             change = "Change, %") |>
  data_color(columns = change, method = "bin",
             bins = c(-Inf, -2, 0, 2, 5, Inf), palette = unname(class_colours),
             autocolor_text = FALSE) |>
  tab_style(style = cell_text(color = "white"),
            locations = cells_body(columns = change, rows = change < -2 | change >= 5)) |>
  tab_style(style = list(cell_text(weight = "bold"),
                         cell_borders(sides = c("top", "bottom"),
                                      color = brand_color_pluck(brand, "primary"),
                                      weight = px(2))),
            locations = cells_body(rows = Country == "European Union")) |>
  tab_source_note("Source: Eurostat (tour_occ_nim)") |>
  theme_brand_gt() |>
  opt_row_striping(row_striping = FALSE) |>
  opt_table_font(font = "Source Sans 3")
```

```{r}
#| label: map-data
europe <- get_eurostat_geospatial(resolution = "20", nuts_level = 0, crs = "3035")
all <- get_eurostat("tour_occ_nim",
  filters = list(unit = "NR", nace_r2 = "I551-I553", c_resid = "TOTAL"))
all <- as.data.frame(all[all$time %in% c(year_ago$time, latest$time), ])
wide <- reshape(all[, c("geo", "time", "values")],
                idvar = "geo", timevar = "time", direction = "wide")
wide$change <- 100 * (wide[[3]] / wide[[2]] - 1)
europe <- merge(europe, wide[, c("geo", "change")], by = "geo")
europe <- europe[!is.na(europe$change) | europe$geo %in% eu_countries$code, ]
europe$class <- cut(europe$change, breaks = c(-Inf, -2, 0, 2, 5, Inf),
                    labels = names(class_colours))
europe$class <- addNA(europe$class)
levels(europe$class)[6] <- "no data"

eu <- europe$geo %in% eu_countries$code
rising <- sum(europe$change[eu] > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
eu_change <- sf::st_drop_geometry(europe[eu & !is.na(europe$change), c("geo", "change")])
up <- eu_change[which.max(eu_change$change), ]
down <- eu_change[which.min(eu_change$change), ]
geo_name <- function(code) label_eurostat(code, dic = "geo")
map_alt <- paste0(
  "Map of Europe. Each country is shaded by the change in nights spent at tourist ",
  "accommodation between ", format(year_ago$time, "%B %Y"), " and ", month,
  ", in five classes: below -2%, -2 to 0%, 0 to 2%, 2 to 5% and 5% or more, ",
  "from dark burgundy for the strongest falls to dark gold for the strongest rises; ",
  "countries without data are grey. In the EU, the largest rise is in ",
  geo_name(up$geo), " (", pct(up$change / 100), ") and the largest fall in ",
  geo_name(down$geo), " (", pct(down$change / 100), "). ",
  "The EU as a whole changed by ", pct(change), ".")
map_headline <- paste(rising, "of the", sum(eu), "EU countries recorded more nights than a year earlier")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-map
#| fig-width: !expr if (knitr::is_html_output()) 7 else 5
#| fig-height: !expr if (knitr::is_html_output()) 6.6 else 5
#| fig-cap: !expr map_headline
#| fig-alt: !expr map_alt
ggplot(europe) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = class), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +
  annotate("label", x = 2.2e6, y = 3.1e6, hjust = 0, vjust = 1,
           label = paste0("EU\n", pct(change)), family = "Source Sans 3",
           fontface = "bold", size = 5, lineheight = 0.9, colour = burgundy,
           fill = brand_color_pluck(brand, "light"), border.colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(class_colours, "no data" = "grey78"), name = NULL,
                    guide = guide_legend(nrow = 1, label.position = "bottom",
                                         keywidth = unit(14, "mm"),
                                         keyheight = unit(3, "mm"))) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(2.1e6, 7.2e6), ylim = c(1.4e6, 5.35e6), datum = NA, expand = FALSE) +
  labs(subtitle = paste("Change in nights spent at tourist accommodation,", month,
                        "compared with", paste0(format(year_ago$time, "%B %Y"), ", %")),
       caption = "Source: Eurostat (tour_occ_nim). Boundaries: (c) EuroGeographics.") +
  theme_nso() +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
```

## Methods and sources {#sec-methods}

**Data.** All figures come from the Eurostat dataset *Nights spent at tourist
accommodation establishments, monthly data* (`tour_occ_nim`), read with the R
package eurostat when this bulletin was produced, on
`r trimws(format(Sys.Date(), "%e %B %Y"))`. They cover hotels, holiday accommodation and
campsites (NACE I55.1 to I55.3) and guests of every country of residence.
Recent months are provisional and can be revised.

**Comparisons.** Each month is compared with the same month a year earlier, which
removes the seasonal pattern without any adjustment. In @fig-trend, the band shows
the lowest and highest value of each month over `r this_year - 4` to
`r this_year - 1`; earlier years are left out because of the Covid-19 pandemic.

**Classes of change.** @tbl-countries and @fig-map share five classes of yearly
change, in %: below -2, -2 to 0, 0 to 2, 2 to 5, and 5 or more.

**Maps.** Country boundaries: GISCO, (c) EuroGeographics.
